title: Lessons from drug revenue life cycles: distributions across modalities and therapeutic areas - Nature Biotechnology
gist: A Harvard analysis of FDA-approved drugs launched between 1995 and 2015 finds that revenue life cycles are unevenly timed and highly concentrated across modalities and therapeutic areas, offering an empirical basis for innovation strategy and drug-pricing policy in a post-Inflation Reduction Act world.

themes.theme: Concentration and timing of drug revenue

insights.claim: An analysis of FDA-approved drugs reveals uneven timing and concentration of revenue life cycles across modalities and therapeutic areas.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: If returns concentrate in a few winners and specific windows, portfolio and pricing strategy should be built around that skew rather than an average drug.
insights.quote: An analysis of FDA-approved drugs reveals uneven timing and concentration of revenue life cycles across modalities and therapeutic areas.

insights.claim: The study measures inter-decile cumulative global net revenues over a 15-year life cycle for all new molecular entities launched between 1995 and 2015, spanning both NDAs and BLAs.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: A 15-year, decile-resolved revenue curve gives investors a concrete template for modeling the lifetime value of an approval by modality.

themes.theme: Policy design under the Inflation Reduction Act

insights.claim: The revenue-lifecycle evidence is offered explicitly to guide innovation strategy and policy design in a post-Inflation Reduction Act world.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: IRA price-negotiation timelines interact with when drugs actually earn revenue, so lifecycle timing determines which modalities are most exposed to the law.
insights.quote: offering evidence to guide innovation strategy and policy design in a post-Inflation Reduction Act world.

insights.claim: Global net revenues are broken out by therapeutic category for all new drugs launched between 1995 and 2015, showing revenue realization differs by disease area.
insights.speaker: Nature Biotechnology
insights.so_what: Therapeutic-area-level revenue curves help investors weight R&D bets toward areas with more durable or front-loaded returns.
